card: Splits the CreateNewBlock_validity unit test into separate, isolated test cases and eliminates mutable state shared across test sections. Currently, miner unit tests reuse an in-memory blockchain and repeatedly mutate a shared transaction object, forcing manual height fixups and introducing order dependencies. The PR separates these into independent tests using a helper to mine the fixture chain and builds transactions declaratively. It modifies only test code.
evidence: Author description: 'The subtests share one chain, so each starts from whatever the previous one left behind, and the caller has to patch Tip()->nHeight between them. Inside TestBasicMining a single CMutableTransaction is reused across all sections... This PR removes both kinds of hidden state.'
problem: CreateNewBlock_validity runs four subtests sequentially across a single 110-block chain, requiring manual height adjustments between tests and creating hidden state dependencies where tests rely on previous side effects. Similarly, TestBasicMining repeatedly mutates a single transaction instance across sections, making individual test cases harder to reason about and isolate.

risk.why: A mistake would only cause false test failures or weakened coverage in unit tests without affecting node operation.

scope_notes: Touches only unit tests in miner testing code.
summary: Splits the unit test CreateNewBlock_validity into independent test cases and removes shared mutable state across test sections. Subtests now initialize their own chain via a shared helper instead of sharing chain state, and TestBasicMining constructs transactions declaratively instead of mutating a single shared transaction object.
uncertainties: Diff was not provided, but commit messages and description clearly describe the scope and changes to miner tests.
